title: Update worsened app
body: New update unfortunately worsened the ”trends” section. The scale of the graphs makes it almost impossible to see and spot trends, which is the most crucial information when tracking symptoms, THE TREND. I dont want to having to flip my phone everytime a want to view a graph/chart, to get in to the detailed graph. Please reverse and change layout back to how it was. I love the app for its simplicity , but this update seriously makes me want to look at other apps. Simplicity is key

title: Doesn’t work, programming wrong
body:
I paid for a year and have used it everyday for 3 months now. Honestly it doesn’t really work. It only shows you correlations. Like I take my anxiety medication when I have anxiety and it only says the medication makes my mood worse. The same with meditation or everything else I might do when I feel bad to make my self feel better. 

Also the mood points each day isn’t the best. If you feel great at 10 AND really bad at 1 one day, it says your mood was 5 that day. So it’s impossible to track mood swings. 
Also if you track that you feel really bad for most of the day, and then you feel better and then a little bit better for a short moment. It will say you felt good that day because you said you felt better two times and you said you felt bad one time. Even though you felt bad for soooo many more hours.
author: testosteronie

title: it’s good, just not for me
body:
It’s a great app! The way you can track mood, energy levels, bowel movements, etc. is awesome. However the layout is quite confusing for me personally. 
The tracking of symptoms like headaches should be similar to the tracking of mood! It’s easier to keep track of them if you can put exact time and what type of headache it is. 
Also it would be great if you could change between the metric system and the imperial system when it comes to amount of water you’ve drank.

The concept of taking care of a bear while tracking your symptoms is a great idea! Making it a little bit like a game can be good for me who has adhd.

I’ll continue my hunt for an app where I can track my symptoms.

title: Too complicated and messy
body:
I’m a person with ADHD and with depression, which means I need to follow my daily patterns to be able to see what makes me feel better and what makes me feel worse, and whether something works for me or not. 

Unfortunately the app is too complicated to keep up with in a longer period of time... I started using it with big enthusiasm, but very soon it got overwhelming due to how chaotic and demanding the structure of the app is.

The privacy policy is not good.

On top of that, I applied for refund twice, and both times I’ve been rejected, which is very questionable. 

To sum up, sadly I don’t think it’s worth the time.
